title: EXP-027 — Button Component Recovery in a Self-Contained Designer Session
objective: Using a self-contained pre-mutation session-establishment approach, create exactly one new User-scoped classic BuildFromScratch Form `FX_ComponentRecoveryLab02`, capture its untouched clean baseline, add exactly one native Toolbox Button, and assign only the component Name `FX_ButtonRecovery02`. Record the exact component Name and the rendered/property-grid Type label before lifecycle testing. Perform exactly one ordinary Designer Save, close the target Form exactly once through its ordinary Form-tab close control, reopen it exactly once through the same Designer's Form-menu recent-forms route, and verify that the same scoped Form recovers a component with Name `FX_ButtonRecovery02` and the exact Type label recorded before close. Treat this as a first observation for this self-contained setup only; do not infer complete component inventory, Caption persistence, Forms-database durability, cache eviction, backend identity, or behavior of other component types.

in_scope: Read EXP-002-R2, EXP-003-R2, EXP-019-R2, EXP-026, recipes/forms/create-basic-form.md, recipes/components/add-component-from-toolbox.md, and recipes/components/configure-basic-component.md before mutation

Launch exactly one Designer only if initial enumeration establishes that no usable Designer page exists in the controlled Playwright browser context; do not attempt an additional Designer while retaining an existing usable Designer in that context

After any permitted session establishment, prove server-backed liveness with a populated supported Select Form dialog, confirm User editing scope, and prove zero case-insensitive Name matches for FX_ComponentRecoveryLab02 with a visible known-existing positive control

Capture an inspected untouched post-creation baseline proving Name, ScopeType, ScopeName, clean target state, and rendered canvas/component state without claiming complete component cardinality
Perform exactly one native Toolbox Button creation operation using the verified placement procedure
Assign only component Name FX_ButtonRecovery02 using the verified Name-edit step; do not perform the Caption-edit or extra Save steps from the broader configuration recipe
Record the exact component Name and exact visible/property-grid Type label before Save, distinguishing Toolbox label Button from a property-grid Type such as PushButton
Perform exactly one ordinary Designer Save after placement and Name setup and prove the target returns clean with component Name and Type unchanged
Close FX_ComponentRecoveryLab02 exactly once through its ordinary Form-tab close control and verify no unsaved-change or unexpected prompt appears
Reopen FX_ComponentRecoveryLab02 exactly once through the same Designer client's Form-menu recent-forms route
Post-reopen verify exact Form identity by Name + ScopeType + ScopeName, clean state, component Name FX_ButtonRecovery02, and exact Type equal to the pre-close recorded Type
Final read-only Select Form case-insensitive Name-filter proof showing exactly one FX_ComponentRecoveryLab02, plus action-count and repository-confinement audit
Capture decisive rendered/property-grid/accessibility evidence under evidence/EXP-027/ and keep conclusions limited to what each capture visibly proves

acceptance_checks.description: Before mutation, enumerate pages in the controlled Playwright browser context and record initial browser/Designer state without inferring the state of other browser processes or windows; if necessary perform no more than one supported pre-mutation session-establishment sequence. Launch one Designer only when that enumeration establishes no usable Designer page in the controlled context. Afterwards prove a live Mongoose workflow with a populated Select Form result, visibly confirm User editing scope, and show Case Sensitive unchecked plus a known-existing positive control and zero case-insensitive Name matches for FX_ComponentRecoveryLab02. Any inherited dirty state must remain untouched.

Create exactly one User-scoped classic BuildFromScratch Form FX_ComponentRecoveryLab02 using the replay-verified fresh-dialog Classic/Build-from-Scratch selection sequence plus the verified basic-form procedure. Evidence must visibly show Save Template unchecked and the loaded clean identity Name=FX_ComponentRecoveryLab02, ScopeType=User, and ScopeName.

Before Button placement, capture an inspected untouched baseline proving the target Form identity, User scope, clean state, and rendered canvas/component state. Record only supported visible inventory information and do not infer complete component cardinality.

Perform exactly one native Toolbox Button creation operation, visibly verify the placed component, assign only Name=FX_ButtonRecovery02 using the verified Name-edit step, and capture decisive property-grid/accessibility evidence of exact Name and exact Type label. No Caption or unrelated property may change.

Perform exactly one ordinary Designer Save after Button placement and Name setup. Evidence must show the target returns clean and the component still has Name=FX_ButtonRecovery02 and the same exact Type recorded in AC-4, with no post-baseline component-property mutation.

Close FX_ComponentRecoveryLab02 exactly once through its ordinary Form-tab close control. Evidence must show the target tab is gone, no unsaved-change or unexpected prompt occurred, no explicit unload was invoked, and the same Designer client remains active.

Reopen FX_ComponentRecoveryLab02 exactly once through the same Designer's Form-menu recent-forms route. Evidence must prove Name + ScopeType + ScopeName, clean state, component Name=FX_ButtonRecovery02, and exact Type equal to AC-4. If the recent-forms entry is unavailable or session establishment is required after mutation, stop blocked without an alternate reopen route.

Final read-only audit must show exactly one case-insensitive Select Form Name match for FX_ComponentRecoveryLab02 and reconcile exactly one Form creation, one Button creation operation, one permitted component Name assignment, one ordinary Save, one target close, and one recent-forms reopen. Repository changes must be confined to the EXP-027 record and evidence/EXP-027/. Classify any successful Button recovery finding no higher than observed because this is an original execution, not a replay.

notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261006-172006-UMJu. Rationale: EXP-026 was blocked before mutation because its acceptance depended on continuity of an inherited Designer client that was subsequently lost; it produced no Button lifecycle finding. The smallest useful next step is therefore not a replay or retry of EXP-026, but a new experiment with an explicitly different documented setup: establish one usable Portal/Web Client/Designer workflow before mutation when needed, then perform the same narrow structural Button test without requiring preservation of a pre-existing Designer lifecycle. This builds on the replay-verified basic-Form, native-component placement, component-configuration Name edit, and fresh Classic/Build-from-Scratch wizard procedures while testing one still-unresolved capability: whether one named native Button component recovers across one ordinary same-Designer Form-tab close/reopen. The result must remain UI-level only and must not be generalized to Caption persistence, database durability, cache eviction, other component types, or internal object identity.
